newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's multi-party assembly votes rules.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's multi-party assembly votes rules.

text.p: Algeria's first multi-party National Assembly on Tuesday voted a set of rules imposing Arabic as the sole language in the assembly and allowing for 12 permanent parliamentary committees.
"The text ensures an efficient running of the assembly," said house speaker Abdelkader Bensalah, quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS.

French is widely spoken in Algeria which gained independence from France in 1962. The imposition of Arabic has angered Berber groups who want their own language to be recognised as official alongside Arabic.
The 135-article set of rules allows political parties to form parliamentary groups provided they muster the support of at least 15 deputies, APS said.
That will force 11 independent deputies and nine from four small opposition parties, including the far left Workers' Party, to join in the five main groups or stay neutral towards them.
The house began its maiden session on June 15, 10 days after the election of its 380 members.
Twenty-nine new deputies took their seats on Tuesday, replacing party colleagues who were appointed ministers in the three-party coalition cabinet, APS said.
Among the newcomers are 22 deputies from the National Democratic Rally (RND), grouping President Liamine Zeroual's supporters.
The others represent the former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) and Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS), which together with the RND form the government.
The RND holds 156 seats in the house, followed by the MPS with 69 and the FLN with 62.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled the first multi-party general election after radical Islamists took a huge lead.
About 60,000 people have died since then in the violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces.
